definitions.explanation: a theory or doctrine developed through academic research and study, typically within a specific field of scholarship

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{学説|がくせつ}が{発表|はっぴょう}された。
examples.english: A new academic theory was published.

examples.japanese: この{学説|がくせつ}は{長年|ながねん}{支持|しじ}されてきた。
examples.english: This theory has been supported for many years.

examples.japanese: {従来|じゅうらい}の{学説|がくせつ}を{覆|くつがえ}す{発見|はっけん}があった。
examples.english: There was a discovery that overturned the conventional theory.

notes:
USAGE:
{学説|がくせつ} emphasizes that a theory comes from academic or scholarly research. It can refer to theories in any academic field, including science, history, linguistics, etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {学説|がくせつ}を{唱|とな}える (to advocate a theory)
- {学説|がくせつ}を{立|た}てる (to establish a theory)
- {学説|がくせつ}を{覆|くつがえ}す (to overturn a theory)
- {有力|ゆうりょく}な{学説|がくせつ} (a leading theory)

RELATED TERMS:
- {理論|りろん} (theory - more general)
- {仮説|かせつ} (hypothesis)
- {定説|ていせつ} (established theory)
